title: Novel Resistance Training–Specific Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale Measuring Repetitions in Reserve
publication: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: 29 adults (mean age 24): 15 experienced squatters and 14 novices.
key_findings: Lifters rated each squat on an RPE scale mapped to repetitions in reserve (RPE 10 = 0 in reserve, RPE 9 = 1, and so on).
Average bar velocity fell as RPE rose, strongly in experienced squatters (r = -0.88) and in novices (r = -0.77).
Experienced squatters were slower and rated a higher RPE at their 1RM than novices; the authors present the scale as practical for adjusting daily load.
methods: Single-session comparison: a 1RM squat, single repetitions at 60, 75 and 90% of 1RM and an 8-repetition set at 70%, with average velocity and RIR-based RPE recorded.
limitations: One exercise, one session and a small sample; it shows how ratings track velocity, not training outcomes.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
